subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw replace the shipped `.deleted.*` / `.reset.*` session archive convention and current retention deletion behavior with a permanent archive model, and what migration or purge policy should existing users get?
rationale: The source proves the current behavior, but changing it affects shipped filenames, session retention, disk-budget cleanup, docs, and downstream tooling expectations, so the product contract needs maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Adopt archive contract with migration
options.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and keep physical purge behind an explicit documented retention policy.

options.title: Keep behavior and clarify docs
options.body: Leave current suffixes and cleanup behavior intact, but document that `.deleted.*` means detached until retention or disk-budget cleanup removes it.

options.title: Split policy from terminology
options.body: Use the narrower retention-semantics issue for naming/config clarity and track no-physical-delete behavior as a separate durability decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt archive contract with migration
recommendation.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and keep physical purge behind an explicit documented retention policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session lifecycle docs and product-surface work make this the best available owner for choosing the public storage contract.
